papers.title: Failure Memories Are Not Neutral: Causal Provenance Effects in Self-Evolving Agents
papers.main_claim: Failure-derived memory provenance is a causal state variable in self-evolving agents: holding task difficulty and semantic guidance fixed, guidance produced from failed trajectories sustains future error more strongly than matched guidance produced from successful trajectories.
existing_evidence: The financial-agent audit reports failure-derived ReasoningBank retrieval accuracy 0.647 over 34 retrievals versus 0.931 over 101 success-derived retrievals.
All ten reported ReasoningBank W->W persistent failures fall in the failure-derived retrieval stratum.
ReasoningBank explicitly constructs success-derived and failure-derived memories with different reflection modes, making provenance an upstream intervention on memory content.
Memory Reward Inflation supplies an independent mechanism by which erroneous or overvalued memories can persist through future reuse.

No DashScope/Qwen embedding credential is available for qwen3.7-text-embedding, so source-faithful ReasoningBank retrieval cannot currently be reconstructed.

papers.title: Noisy Rewards Write Noisy Memories: Reward Error as a Variance Amplifier in Self-Improving Agents
papers.main_claim: Proxy reward noise becomes persistent state when reward-conditioned memory construction rewrites the interpretation of an identical trajectory, and this state perturbation amplifies downstream run variance under memory reuse.
existing_evidence: The fragility study reports substantial multi-run variance and explicitly treats proxy LLM reward as a noisy confound, using ground-truth reward in its main memory construction experiments.

Released ReasoningBank code maps score=1 to a success-reflection prompt and score=0 to a failure-reflection prompt, so one reward bit changes the memory-construction objective for the same trajectory.

The paired F0 intervention holds each released trajectory fixed and changes only the reward-conditioned reflection mode; all 4 complete pairs change normalized memory content and title sets, with mean token-set Jaccard distance 0.734789.

A disjoint eight-trajectory prompt-perturbation control uses same-mode paraphrases whose lexical perturbation exceeds the released reward-mode prompt difference; between-mode memory distance is 0.699949 versus 0.594971 within mode, giving mean paired excess 0.104978 with exact sign-flip p=0.0078125.
Memory Reward Inflation independently shows that proxy reward errors can accumulate through memory reuse.

papers.title: Temporal Skills Are a Causal Bottleneck in Evolving Time-Series Agents
papers.main_claim: Reusable temporal and exogenous-context procedures are the causal bottleneck behind a large class of recurring TimeSage-EV failures, and targeted skill injection removes these failures beyond generic skill retrieval.
existing_evidence: TimeSage-EV reports recurring temporal-validity and exogenous-context failures across model tiers.
TimeSage-1.0 adds a reusable skill library while keeping the baseline harness aligned, and the skill-memory condition improves aggregate benchmark performance.
The released paper Appendix defines explicit induct_skill and retrieve_skill interfaces, giving a concrete intervention surface for targeted temporal procedures.
